skill.name: analytics-tracking
skill.description: Design and audit event models, conversion definitions, data quality checks, attribution rules, and governance for reliable analytics decisions.
skill.summary: Turn business questions into validated tracking plans and trustworthy measurement systems.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by Markdown and analytics terminology in SKILL.md. The skill contains advisory measurement guidance, with no executable commands, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or data-exfiltration intent.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 229-231 are a fenced Markdown example containing only the event-name pattern object_action[_context]. They contain no Ruby, shell backticks, or executable command.
Line 304 advises avoiding multiple Google Tag Manager containers. It concerns analytics configuration and performs no host, network, user, or process reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Unclear events and inconsistent conversions make analytics difficult to trust. This skill creates decision-focused measurement plans, quality scores, validation steps, and governance guidance.
actual_capabilities: Scores measurement readiness across six weighted categories and assigns a clear readiness band.
Designs event taxonomies and naming conventions that connect tracked actions to business decisions.
Creates tracking plans with event descriptions, properties, triggers, and supported decisions.
Defines meaningful conversions and documents counting rules across analytics tools.
Recommends validation, attribution, privacy, ownership, and maintenance practices for GA4 and GTM.
limitations: Provides guidance only and does not connect to analytics platforms or inspect live event data.
Requires business questions, current events, tools, and compliance constraints for a useful assessment.
Readiness scores depend on the accuracy and completeness of supplied evidence.
Does not replace environment-specific testing, privacy counsel, or regulatory review.

use_cases.title: Plan Product Analytics
use_cases.description: Create a decision-focused event model for onboarding, activation, feature use, and retention.

use_cases.title: Repair Campaign Measurement
use_cases.description: Standardize conversions, UTM rules, attribution context, and reporting signals across acquisition channels.

use_cases.title: Audit Tracking Quality
use_cases.description: Find duplicate events, missing properties, consent gaps, unclear ownership, and unreliable conversion counts.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Analytics Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess our analytics readiness for [product]. We use [tools] and track [events]. Score each category, explain gaps, and recommend the first fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a structured review of an existing measurement setup.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Tracking Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tracking plan for [journey]. Our decisions are [decisions]. Define events, properties, triggers, conversions, counting rules, owners, and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Translate business questions into an implementation-ready measurement plan.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Event Inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this event inventory: [inventory]. Map each event to a decision, identify duplication and PII risks, then propose a cleaner taxonomy and validation plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing event model with unclear or excessive tracking.

prompt_templates.title: Design Cross-Platform Measurement
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced measurement strategy for [business model] across [domains and devices]. Include GA4 and GTM notes, attribution rules, consent states, ownership, testing, and governance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate complex measurement requirements across platforms and teams.

output_examples.input: Review a SaaS signup funnel using GA4 and GTM with duplicate form events and unclear conversion counting.
output: Readiness score: 61, Unreliable. Main gaps are duplicate firing, unclear ownership, and inconsistent conversion rules.
Priority action: define signup_completed as the conversion, document once-per-user counting, and test consent, mobile, and browser states.
Tracking plan: pricing_viewed supports offer analysis; form_started supports abandonment analysis; signup_completed supports acquisition and activation decisions.

output_examples.input: Create measurement guidance for an online store that uses inconsistent UTMs and treats product views as conversions.
output: Use purchase_completed as the primary conversion and keep product_viewed as an intent signal.
Adopt lowercase UTM values, consistent separators, central documentation, and rules that preserve the original source.
Validate order values, duplicate purchases, consent states, mobile behavior, and cross-domain attribution before reporting performance.

best_practices: Start with the decisions and actions that each metric must support.
Prefer a small set of accurate events with documented properties and owners.
Validate duplicate firing, consent behavior, attribution, mobile, and browser coverage before using results.
anti_patterns: Do not track events without a defined decision or responsible owner.
Do not classify page views, button clicks, or form starts as completed conversions.
Do not collect PII, unrestricted free text, or duplicate automatic properties.

faq.question: Which analytics tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: It provides general guidance and includes specific recommendations for GA4, Google Tag Manager, UTMs, and common product analytics platforms.

faq.question: Does this skill install tracking code?
faq.answer: No. It designs and audits measurement plans but does not access platforms, publish containers, or modify application code.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide business decisions, user journeys, current events, conversions, tools, known data issues, owners, and compliance constraints.

faq.question: How is measurement readiness scored?
faq.answer: The score weights decision alignment, event clarity, data integrity, conversion quality, attribution context, and governance.

faq.question: Can it help prevent privacy problems?
faq.answer: It identifies PII, consent, minimization, deletion, and retention concerns, but qualified experts must confirm legal compliance.

faq.question: What happens when the setup scores poorly?
faq.answer: The skill stops optimization guidance, explains the reliability gaps, and recommends remediation before decisions depend on the data.
